questions.text: How do you decide what to automate and what to leave for manual testing?

follow_up_suggestions.text: Can you give an example of a test you chose not to automate, and why?
How do you judge the value of an automated test over time?

scoring_rubric.2: Automates everything or nothing, without reasons
scoring_rubric.3: Weighs frequency, risk and cost of each test
scoring_rubric.4: Applies a clear test strategy across unit, API and UI levels
scoring_rubric.5: Also reviews test value over time and retires weak tests

questions.text: Tell me about a flaky test you dealt with. How did you find the cause and make the test reliable?

follow_up_suggestions.text: What did you change in the test or in the application?
How did you stop the flakiness from coming back?

scoring_rubric.2: Retries the test without finding the cause
scoring_rubric.3: Finds a timing or data cause and fixes it
scoring_rubric.4: Improves waiting, isolation and test data, and checks the fix
scoring_rubric.5: Adds monitoring for flakiness and shares the fix as a team practice

questions.text: How do you design API tests so they stay useful when the API changes?

follow_up_suggestions.text: What do you assert on: status codes, schemas, business rules, or all three?
How do you test error responses, not only successful ones?

scoring_rubric.3: Asserts responses and key business rules
scoring_rubric.4: Uses schema checks, test data control and error cases
scoring_rubric.5: Also uses contract tests to catch breaking changes early

questions.text: A release is due tomorrow and a critical bug was found in exploratory testing. Walk me through what you would do.

follow_up_suggestions.text: How would you decide whether the release should be delayed?
Who would you tell, and what would you tell them?

scoring_rubric.2: Reports the bug without assessing impact
scoring_rubric.3: Assesses severity, reproduces the bug and informs the team
scoring_rubric.4: Gives a clear go or no-go recommendation with risks
scoring_rubric.5: Also proposes a targeted regression check and a follow-up to prevent recurrence

questions.text: How do you keep test runs fast enough for developers to rely on them in every pull request?

follow_up_suggestions.text: Which tests run on every pull request, and which run later?
How do you run tests in parallel without sharing state?

scoring_rubric.2: Suggests running fewer tests without a plan
scoring_rubric.3: Splits fast and slow suites and runs them in CI
scoring_rubric.4: Uses parallelism, isolation and test data strategy
scoring_rubric.5: Measures run times, sets budgets and continuously optimises the pipeline
